answer: Each agent claims one cedar stand, locks an 80-credit bond, and files one core sample at the inlet, sealed with a numbered thread tag on its registry ledge. One sample per key; reused tags are rejected. An auditor re-weighs the sample against the cedar table; mismatch or reuse burns the bond. The k-th sample costs 33+7(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 7026, and 1000 fakes pay 3,529,500 and lock 80,000. A rented-sample ring fails: one tag cannot serve two keys, and a borrowed core repeats its fingerprint. An honest agent pays 33 once and recovers the bond after audit.
